title: SharePoint admin center: Data access governance report of sites a group can access
notes: claim 70: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
the verifier wrote "hold" but listed no blocker and fewer than three majors; the claims decide, so the page is not held
summary: The rollout statements, licensing requirements and six control surfaces are supported. The impact rationale nevertheless promises no change for site owners and group members when Microsoft has not stated the arrival default. Statements ruling out remediation also go beyond the documented reporting workflow and should be narrowed.

claims.claim: Group reports exclude permissions inherited through nested-group membership.

claims.claim: The user report shows direct access and indirect access through group membership for named users.
claims.quote: For users, the report includes counts of items shared directly with the user and items accessible indirectly through group membership.

claims.claim: The group report supports a ZIP download containing CSV files for all included groups.
claims.quote: Select Download report for all groups in a group report, or Download detailed report in a user report, to get a ZIP file containing CSV files for all recipients included in the report.

claims.claim: The report finds exposure but does not fix it.
claims.quote: Searched: "site permissions for users or groups" "remediation" "permissions"; "group permission state report" "read-only" "permissions". Read the users/groups report, DAG overview and PowerShell guide; they describe reporting, not an explicit no-remediation guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace 'The report finds exposure; it does not fix it.' with 'The report lists sites accessible to the selected group and the extent of that access.' The report page at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-site-permissions-users-report states this narrower behavior.

claims.claim: The group option is at SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users or groups > View reports > Create report > Create report for > Groups.
claims.quote: From the Data access governance landing page, select View reports under Site permissions for users or groups. ... Select Create report to generate your report. ... Under Create report for, select Users or Groups, then select Next.

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide documents Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name <name> -TargetGroups <groups> to generate the group report.
claims.quote:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight `
    -ReportEntity PermissionsReport `
    -ReportType Snapshot `
    -Workload SharePoint `
    -Name "GroupPermissionsReport" `
    -TargetGroups $groups

claims.claim: TargetGroups takes group objects returned by Get-MgGroup.
claims.quote: Retrieve the groups with Get-MgGroup, then pass the returned group objects directly to the TargetGroups parameter.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: group report; Open questions
claims.claim: The Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight cmdlet reference currently omits TargetGroups even though the PowerShell guide documents it.
claims.quote: Searched: "Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight" "TargetGroups". Read the full Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight reference and its parameter sets: no TargetGroups. Read the PowerShell guide's Generate a group permission state report section, which documents TargetGroups.

claims.claim: Data access governance reports are reached through SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance.
claims.quote: In the left pane, expand Reports and then select Data access governance.

claims.claim: Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity <entity> lists Data access governance reports for the specified entity.
claims.quote:
Lists various 'Data Access Governance' (DAG) reports in SharePoint admin center.
Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide documents Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport for checking user and group permission reports.
claims.quote:
Use the following command to check user and group permission reports:

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference documents Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name <name> -UserPrincipalNames <UPNs> for the user report.
claims.quote:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide uses UserEmailList rather than the reference's UserPrincipalNames spelling.
claims.quote: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name "UserSharePointReport" -UserEmailList "a@contoso.com","b@contoso.com"

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide says UserEmailList requires user principal names.
claims.quote: While the parameter is named UserEmailList, the report requires user principal names.

claims.claim: The site permissions for your organization report must be generated at least once before running the user or group report.
claims.quote: Review these important details before creating your first report: ... Make sure that the site permissions for your organization report is generated at least once.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for the group-report capability, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "site permissions for users or groups" "default"; "group permission" "report" "automatic" SharePoint. Read roadmap, MC1540348, users/groups report, DAG overview and PowerShell guide; none states an enablement or enforcement default.

claims.claim: Running the report is an administrator-chosen workflow rather than a mandatory action in Microsoft's notice.
claims.quote: Select Create report to generate your report. ... Select Create and run to trigger the creation of report.

claims.claim: Site owners and group members see no change from the feature's arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: "data access governance" "group" "no impact" "users"; SharePoint site permissions users groups snapshot report enabled default automatically permissions changes site owners group members. Read MC1540348, roadmap, users/groups report and DAG overview; no no-change guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: "Low. Microsoft's notice names SharePoint administrators as the people affected; no source says existing site permissions change on arrival." This removes the unsupported arrival guarantee and agrees with defaultState: unknown.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls: remedial options
claims.claim: Restricted access control, the Change history report and Site access review are not part of, or controls over, this report.
claims.quote: Searched: "site permissions for users or groups" "Restricted access control" "Change history" "Site access review". Read DAG overview, users/groups report and PowerShell guide; they name follow-up actions but do not explicitly state this exclusion.
claims.fix: Delete ', and none is part of this report' from Risk assessment: Security & identity and '; none is a control over this report' from Governance controls. Keep the preceding statements naming Microsoft's documented remedial options.
